rationale: Empirical quantitative study in Dakar, Senegal examining the privatization of sewage treatment center management (a utility/infrastructure ownership and governance mechanism) using administrative records (2009-2018), household survey data, and DHS data, measuring household sanitation service prices (affordability) and legal sanitary waste dumping volumes. Meets all inclusion criteria (C1-C4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and plain wording of Criterion 2 are clearly satisfied because privatization of sewage treatment center management is an explicit ownership/contractual governance structure affecting household sanitation service affordability and legal desludging access.

evidence_quotes.quote: Privatization of a public good (the management of sewage treatment centers in Dakar, Senegal) leads to an increase in the productivity of downstream sewage dumping companies and a decrease in downstream prices of the services they provide to households.

We use the universe of legal dumping of sanitation waste from May 2009 to May 2018 to show that legal dumping increased substantially following privatization-on average an increase of 74%, or an increase of about 1640 trips to treatment centers each month.
Household-level survey data shows that downstream prices of legal sanitary dumping decreased by 5% following privatization
